content.user_title: Build Reliable Temporal Workflows in Python
content.value_statement: Distributed workflows are difficult to make deterministic, retryable, and observable. This skill provides focused Python SDK guidance for design, testing, and production operations.
actual_capabilities: Designs deterministic workflows with Temporal Python decorators and workflow-safe APIs.
Defines activities, execution models, retry policies, timeouts, heartbeats, and cancellation handling.
Plans signals, queries, child workflows, sagas, and compensation logic.
Creates testing strategies using time skipping, activity mocks, error injection, and replay validation.
Reviews worker deployment, scaling, versioning, monitoring, tracing, and graceful shutdown practices.
Identifies common determinism, idempotency, payload, concurrency, and task queue mistakes.
limitations: Provides guidance and generated examples but does not run a Temporal cluster.
Cannot validate production histories, infrastructure settings, or workload behavior without project inputs.
Does not replace official SDK documentation or environment-specific security review.
Requires clarification when task queues, retry requirements, payloads, or failure semantics are unspecified.

use_cases.title: Create a Durable Order Workflow
use_cases.description: Design an order process with retryable activities, timeouts, and compensation for failed payments or inventory reservations.

use_cases.title: Test Long-Running Business Processes
use_cases.description: Plan time-skipping tests, activity mocks, error injection, and replay checks for workflows lasting days or months.

use_cases.title: Prepare Workers for Production
use_cases.description: Review worker scaling, task queues, graceful shutdown, observability, and version rollout for a production deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Temporal Concept
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the difference between a Temporal workflow and an activity in Python. Include determinism, retries, and one practical example.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Temporal Python workflow for [process]. Define inputs, activities, timeouts, retries, signals, queries, and failure behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a new durable business process.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Temporal Python workflow for determinism, idempotency, blocking calls, timeout coverage, retry safety, and payload limits. Explain each finding.
prompt_templates.scenario: Assess an existing workflow before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Production Evolution
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production migration plan for changing [workflow]. Cover replay compatibility, worker versioning, rollout, rollback, monitoring, and validation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Evolve running workflows without breaking history replay.

output_examples.input: Design retry behavior for a payment activity.
output: Classify network failures as retryable and validation failures as permanent.
Set a bounded exponential backoff policy and a total activity timeout.
Use an idempotency key so retries cannot create duplicate charges.
Add compensation behavior when later order steps fail.

output_examples.input: Create a testing checklist for a month-long approval workflow.
output: Use time skipping to exercise every deadline without waiting.
Mock approval activities and inject transient and permanent failures.
Test duplicate and late signals for idempotent behavior.
Replay representative histories before releasing workflow changes.

output_examples.output: The review covers task queue alignment, registered workflows, concurrency limits, graceful shutdown, health metrics, tracing, and compatible rollout procedures.

best_practices: Keep workflow logic deterministic and move external calls into activities.
Make activities idempotent and define explicit retry, timeout, heartbeat, and cancellation behavior.
Test failures, compensation, time progression, and replay compatibility before deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not call external services or use nondeterministic system APIs directly inside workflows.
Do not run blocking libraries in async activities because they can stall the event loop.
Do not deploy workflow changes without replay testing and a compatible versioning strategy.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps design Temporal workflows, activities, workers, tests, and production operating practices with the Python SDK.

faq.question: Does it connect to a Temporal cluster?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples but does not connect to or modify a cluster.

faq.question: Can it review existing workflow code?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the relevant code and requirements for a review of determinism, retries, timeouts, idempotency, and deployment risks.

faq.question: Does it cover workflow testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers time skipping, mocked activities, error injection, integration tests, and replay validation.

faq.question: Can it help with saga patterns?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan ordered activities, failure handling, and compensation steps for distributed transactions.

faq.question: What information improves the result?
faq.answer: Provide the business process, failure rules, task queues, expected duration, payloads, dependencies, and deployment constraints.
